title: fix(enter): drop duplicate redirectUri validation on metadata update
author: iotserver24
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #11451

The metadata-update route validated `redirectUris` twice: Zod `UrlWithSchemeSchema` at the request boundary, then `validateRedirectUriFormat` again in the handler. Anything invalid never reached the second check.

This keeps the handler loop as the single check (same idiom as create) so the precise `HTTPException` message is what the client gets.

**Verify**
- `npx vitest run test/integration/api-keys.test.ts` — 36/36 pass
- includes `rejects unsafe redirectUris during metadata updates` (still 400)

gist.headline: One gate, better signs
gist.blurb: Redirect URI checks now take the same path during API-key metadata updates as they do at creation. Fewer duplicate gates; clearer notes when a URL does not belong in the garden.
gist.summary: Removed duplicate redirectUris validation from the API-key metadata-update request boundary so the handler's existing validation returns the same precise HTTPException messages used during API-key creation.
gist.impact: Developers updating API-key metadata still get a 400 for unsafe redirectUris, now with the consistent, specific redirect URI format error from the shared handler check.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy API-key garden gate has one clear signpost instead of two overlapping guards: Polli, wearing a tiny groundskeeper hat, tidies duplicate URL-check signs while a safe vine-shaped redirect path leads into a glowing terminal garden. The scene represents consistent validation and clearer client errors, with code-plants and a small 400 error note as supporting details.
